name: Landing
description: The pause in a stair, and the place where the upper floor's privacy gradient is actually set. A landing that is merely a corner is a fault; a landing with a window is the cheapest good room in the house.

history.note: The dog-leg stair with a half-pace landing arrives in England in the seventeenth century and replaces the newel stair. It is what makes a stair a piece of architecture rather than a device, and the window on the half-pace is the reason a Georgian stair hall is lit at all.

dimensions.critical_dimension: Landing depth must be at least the stair width, which is code and also the point at which two people can pass. Below that it is a turn, not a landing.

furniture.note: The half-pace window seat is the single best return on square footage in a traditional plan.

daylight.orientation: North is fine and often best — the light is even and the stair is not a room you linger in for warmth.

aspect.basis: North is fine and often best

daylight.note: A tall window on the half-pace lights two storeys at once, which is why it is worth more than its area suggests and why the Palladian window ended up there so often.

must_adjoin.why: By definition. VERTICAL_OK added 24 Aug 2026 (OQ 59, using OQ 57's mechanism): a landing is the top of a stair, and the stair hall it belongs to is on the storey BELOW it. Read as a same-floor rule this could only be satisfied by a house with a second stair hall upstairs, so every two-storey parti with a landing failed it -- which is the rule asking for the one thing a landing structurally cannot have.

must_not_adjoin.why: A bedroom door opening directly onto a landing that is visible from the hall below removes the privacy buffer the upper floor depends on.

servicing.ventilation: The stack of the house: a landing window that opens is the cheapest summer ventilation available.
servicing.electrical: Switched from both floors, which is code and is still got wrong.

style_variation.note: The half-pace window is often the most elaborate on the house — a Palladian or Venetian window on the rear elevation lighting the stair.
Landing seat with storage beneath, treated as joinery.

code.requirement: Landing depth not less than the stair width, minimum 36 in

sources: Waterman, The Dwellings of Colonial America
